hook.evidence: Highlights IoT growth and the promise of OWC technologies.

gap.evidence: Notes lack of a top-down OWC IoT survey spanning terrestrial, underwater, biomedical, and underground domains.

yes_but.evidence: Prior OWC surveys focus on subsets; this work unifies multiple IoT domains.

scope_boundary.evidence: Focus on OWC systems, networks, standards, and applications across IoTT/IoWT/IoBT/IoGT.

rhetorical_moves_global.reader_contract_pattern: Motivate/gap; give OWC preliminaries; cover IoTT, IoWT, IoBT, IoGT each with summaries; conclude with open problems.

branches: OWC IoBT (RF vs OWC, on/off-body, transdermal, SLIPT)

visuals_tables.layout_logic: Preliminaries include taxonomy/standard figures; each IoT domain section includes application figures and product/testbed visuals plus summary tables; consistent summaries end each domain.

figures.purpose: depict OWC system/network taxonomy and IoT domains

tables.purpose: summarize OWC standards or domain-specific comparisons

lesson_blocks.lesson: Standardization and system/network taxonomies set constraints for all domains.
OWC IoTT design differs between agriculture and smart-city deployments; COTS options exist but gaps remain.
Opto-acoustic hybrids and testbeds highlight feasibility but underwater challenges persist.
On/off-body vs transdermal OWC requires different power/channel models; SLIPT enables self-sustainability.
Underground OWC relies on specialized channel models and localization techniques; applications are early-stage.

synthesis.aha_moment: Using a consistent domain-by-domain template (taxonomy -> challenges/testbeds -> lessons) makes a broad OWC IoT landscape navigable.

style.section_openers_pattern: Introduce domain/topic, enumerate subcategories, close with summary/insights/open problems.
